title: Who Did It: Passive Sentences in History

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18: *La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento*. The participle agrees with the subject, and *por* names who did the action. History writing uses it all the time, because what was done matters more than who did it. The founding of Cartagena, its walls and the story of Palenque all fit the pattern.

sections.title: Ser + past participle on this topic
rows: Cartagena fue fundada en 1533 por Pedro de Heredia.
*fue fundada*: singular feminine, to agree with *Cartagena*; *por* names who founded it
Las murallas fueron construidas para defender la ciudad.
*fueron construidas*: plural feminine, to agree with *las murallas*
El palenque fue fundado por personas que huyeron de la esclavitud.
*fundado*: masculine singular, to agree with *el palenque*
Los tambores fueron traídos de África.
*fueron traídos*: plural masculine; no *por* when the actor is not named

items.spanish: La ciudad fue atacada por los ingleses en 1586.
items.english: The city was attacked by the English in 1586.

items.spanish: Las fortalezas fueron construidas entre los siglos XVI y XVIII.
items.english: The fortresses were built between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries.

items.spanish: Palenque fue reconocido por la UNESCO en 2005.
items.english: Palenque was recognised by UNESCO in 2005.

sections.content: With *ser* the participle always agrees with the subject: *fundada*, *construidas*, *traídos*. You know the *se* passive from B1 Unit 6 (*se construyeron las murallas*): use it when nobody in particular did the action, and *ser* + participle when you want to name the actor or stress the result.
